title: Significant Other AI: Identity, Memory, and Emotional Regulation as Long-Term Relational Intelligence
abstract: arXiv:2512.00418v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Significant Others (SOs) stabilize identity, regulate emotion, and support narrative meaning-making, yet many people today lack access to such relational anchors. Recent advances in large language models and memory-augmented AI raise the question of whether artificial systems could support some of these functions. translated_title: 重要他人AI：身份、记忆与情绪调节作为长期关系智能
translated_abstract: 重要他人（SOs）能够稳定身份认同、调节情绪并支持叙事意义构建，然而当今许多人缺乏此类关系锚点。大型语言模型和记忆增强型AI的最新进展引发了人工系统能否支持其中某些功能的疑问。然而，现有的共情AI仍是被动且短期的，缺乏自传体记忆、身份建模、预测性情绪调节和叙事连贯性。本手稿引入重要他人人工智能（SO-AI）作为关系AI的新领域。它综合心理学和社会学理论来定义SO功能，并推导出SO-AI的需求，包括身份意识、长期记忆、主动支持、叙事共建和伦理边界执行。本文提出一个概念架构，包括拟人化界面、关系认知模块等。
tldr: 本文提出了重要他人人工智能（SO-AI）这一新领域，通过整合心理学和社会学理论，为AI赋予身份意识、长期记忆、主动情绪调节和叙事共建能力，以弥补现有共情AI的短期被动缺陷，并提出了包含拟人化界面和伦理边界的概念架构。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Significant Other Artificial Intelligence (SO-AI) as a new domain of relational AI, synthesizing psychological and sociological theories to equip AI with identity awareness, long-term memory, proactive emotional regulation, and narrative co-construction, addressing the short-term reactive limitations of existing empathic AIs and proposing a conceptual architecture with anthropomorphic interface and ethical boundaries.
